subject: Renewal planning: usage cascade + rollover / term options
messages:
From: Anita Lopez <anita@brightgrid.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal review: Q2 spend spike & rollover options

Hi Irene / team,

We closed out Q2 and I wanted to flag a couple of items ahead of our renewal discussion: 
- Q2 token spend was ~2.8M tokens, a ~42% jump driven by a new image-analysis augmentation feature we rolled into a handful of flows.
- Latency/p99 has been stable, but cost-per-inference went up because of longer contexts and more streaming.

We are evaluating whether to: (a) extend current term with a higher committed capacity and a rollover clause, (b) move to a month-to-month burst model for the new feature, or (c) do a mixed approach with committed baseline + burst credits.

Can your team share a short ROI recap (cost per 100k tokens by model family, expected unit economics change if we add 1.5x committed capacity, and proposed rollover mechanics)? We have a procurement review next Thursday and would like preliminary options.

Attachment: BrightGrid_Q2_usage_summary.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Lopez
Head of Procurement, BrightGrid
procurement@brightgrid.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review: Q2 spend spike & rollover options

Hi Anita — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. Quick acknowledgement: we can run a concise ROI model and present 2–3 term options ahead of your procurement review.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Ben will pull a token-cost breakdown by model family and context length (today vs. Q2).
- I’ll map those against committed-capacity scenarios (1.0x / 1.5x / 2.0x) and include burst-credit pricing and rollover mechanics.
- Karthik will outline SLA/latency impacts for larger commitments and share potential credits for latency-sensitive SLAs.

Can we lock a 30-minute sync on Thursday at 10:30 PT? If that conflicts with your review calendar we’ll send options.

Best,
Irene

- Current effective unit cost (weighted across models in BrightGrid account): $0.0009 per token.
- Top 3 generators contributing to spike: image-aug (48%), long-context summarizer (23%), reranker (9%).
- If BrightGrid moves to 1.5x committed capacity and enables prefix caching for the image-aug flow, modeled cost reduction is ~24% on incremental tokens.

From: Anita Lopez <anita@brightgrid.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review: Q2 spend spike & rollover options

Thanks — that is helpful. A couple clarifying items before the call: 
- For the 1.5x committed scenario, do you have an example of how rollover would work at quarter-end (carry-forward limits, expiration)?
- We need to understand any required term amendment language that would permit automatic model-switch fallback if a legacy model is deprecated mid-term. Please flag legal-rate risks.

Also, can you include an option which is a 12-month term with quarterly rollover (max 25% carry-forward) and a second option that is an 18-month term with 50% carry-forward but steeper upfront commit discount? Our procurement prefers discrete examples.

Uploaded: BrightGrid_updated_MAPlan.xlsx (xlsx) — includes target renewal dates and internal stakeholder list.

—Anita

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Anita Lopez <anita@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review: Q2 spend spike & rollover options

Anita — appreciate the clarity and the MA Plan. We reviewed and prepared three discrete options (summary below) and attached a short one-pager for procurement + a proposed term amendment template. Full ROI workbook and SLA table attached to the HubSpot deal.

Summary (attached one-pager):
1) 12-month term — baseline commit = current run-rate * 1.2; quarterly rollover up to 25%; 12% unit discount on committed tokens; burst credits available at 1.6x baseline at standard overage rate.
2) 18-month term — baseline commit = current run-rate * 1.5; rollover up to 50% per quarter; 18% unit discount; includes one-time onboarding credit and priority capacity windows for scheduled trainings.
3) Flexible quarterly — 3-month rolling baseline with a capped burst pool and higher per-token rate; recommended if you want minimal term exposure and fast elasticity.

Legal/operational notes: automatic fallback to a compatible model family is permitted; we will include a 45-day deprecation notice and optional migration credits in the amendment. Karthik: SLA credit examples are in the attached doc.

Action items / next steps:
- We’ll send the one-pager + term amendment PDF to your procurement by end of day (sent).
- If procurement agrees to review option 1 or 2, we’ll prepare the DocuSign with selected term and pre-filled MA Plan fields.
- Proposed meeting: Mon 25 Jun, 10:30 PT to finalize selection and signature path — want me to lock that?

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Irene
